title: On Implying that nobody was to blame
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：imply　|　正文 361 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 imply 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the keeper ① implied that nobody was to blame for the whole place, and every traveller in the tower said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the keeper ② implies that nobody was to blame without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ imply that nobody was to blame at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ implied that nobody was to blame before — a line in the calendar for January 1943 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Implying that nobody was to blame for the whole place, the keeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the clock at the far stair, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ imply a bill nobody had counted on without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Imply a bill nobody had counted on at once and never mention it again.

By 1956 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the calendar, and a new traveller from the next tower ⑧ implies a bill nobody had counted on for the whole place every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stair, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ implied that nobody was to blame again when nobody else would.

⑩ To imply that nobody was to blame, my mother said in 1961, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the tower remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the tower forgets, somebody implies that nobody was to blame without a word of thanks again and somebody must imply that nobody was to blame for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 暗示（一般过去式 implied that nobody was to blame：1949 年守夜人头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 暗示（一般现在 implies that nobody was to blame：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 暗示（不定式 to imply that nobody was to blame：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 暗示（过去完成时 had implied that nobody was to blame：1943 年一月的年历上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 暗示（动名词 implying that nobody was to blame 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 意味着（imply a bill nobody had counted on：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去意味着一笔谁也没算进去的开销）
G. v. 意味着（imply a bill nobody had counted on：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 暗示（后段两处：新来的过路人照例 implies a bill nobody had counted on，而母亲又一次 implied that nobody was to blame）

answers.why: imply 意为“暗示”，1949 年守夜人替所有人暗示暗示谁也不該受责，那是钟楼里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 implied。
imply 意为“暗示”，自那以后守夜人不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 implies。
imply 意为“暗示”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯暗示暗示谁也不該受责”，此处为不定式 to imply that nobody was to blame。
imply 意为“暗示”，年历里 一月 那行字说明早在 1956 年之前就有人暗示过，故用过去完成时 had implied。
imply 意为“暗示”，守夜人说“暗示暗示谁也不該受责这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 implying that nobody was to blame 作主语。
imply 意为“意味着”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去意味着一笔谁也没算进去的开销”，should ever 之后用原形 imply a bill nobody had counted on。
imply 意为“意味着”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻意味着一笔谁也没算进去的开销（imply a bill nobody had counted on at once），以后再也不要提起。
imply 意为“暗示”，新来的过路人每个年头都照例意味着一笔谁也没算进去的开销，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 implies。
imply 意为“暗示”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人暗示暗示谁也不該受责，用一般过去式 implied 叙述。
imply 意为“暗示”，结尾那句是母亲 1961 年的话：要暗示暗示谁也不該受责，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和钟楼记住的那一件。

守夜人说过，替所有人暗示暗示谁也不該受责这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（implying that nobody was to blame 作主语）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 imply 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the keeper implied that nobody was to blame for the whole place, and nobody in the tower forgot it.
Even now the keeper implies that nobody was to blame without a word of thanks whenever the tower asks.
Implying that nobody was to blame for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever imply a bill nobody had counted on without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next tower implies a bill nobody had counted on for the whole place every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother implied that nobody was to blame again, and the tower remembered that half.
